text:
maria: quick heads-up — I regressed KV resident set on the longctx workload when we enabled cross-request prefix handoff. Profiling shows steady mem growth over ~30m.
sam: can you paste the flame graph link? also what commit/flag flipped?
maria: flame: https://perf.internal/graphs/3519876543 — flag is ENABLE_PREFIX_HANDOFF=1, canary on runtime-canary-5
ops-bot: alert: kv-residency > 8.2GB on runtime-canary-5 :warning:
jun: interesting. do we know if it's fragmentation (many small pages) or actual sticky refs keeping pages alive?
maria: preliminary heapmap looks like many small 256B allocations tied to KV meta objects; but there are also large contiguous pages not evicted. suspect key canonicalization is creating near-duplicates.
liam: could be our key derivation. right now we include full prompt prefix bytes + tenant salt. that makes slightly different prefixes for near-identical contexts.
sam: if keys vary too much, handoff will spread hot prefixes across slots and reduce reuse -> more hotset churn and slower eviction.
maria: proposal: canonicalize prefix key by hashing only the first 64 tokens + tenant id and append a 4-bit prefix-length bucket. example:

```
# pseudo
prefix_key = sha256(tenant_id || first_64_tokens_utf8)[:16] || bucket(prefix_len)
```

that should collapse near-duplicates while still being tenant-isolated.
jun: +1. also suggests we add a sampling prefetch heuristic: when we see a new key that matches existing bucket, prefetch the top 3 likely continuation keys into hot cache (cheap async).
liam: two caveats: 1) need to prove it reduces fragmentation vs causing more false positives; 2) check CPU cost of sha256 on hot paths; maybe do hashing in runtime kernel offload.
maria: perf notes from canary: tail latency increased 12% under steady RPS with handoff enabled; median unchanged. memory + CPU both rose.
sam: quick experiment plan: (A) revert handoff on canary to confirm regression; (B) run variant with canonicalized key hashing + prefetch sampler; (C) measure eviction churn and resident set. assign: maria(A,B) sam(C) jun(profile scripts) liam(kernel offload feasibility)
maria: I'll post a small repro harness and the flame graph snapshot in #eng-runtime so people can iterate. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
